summary: This is a small data-holding class that represents one player on a sports team, storing a name, a playing position, and the number of goals they have scored. Once you have a list of these objects, stream pipelines can group them by position and pick out the top scorers.

lines.text: The field is `private` so nothing outside the class can reach in and change it, and `final` so it can only be set once, in the constructor.
Goal counts are whole numbers, so `int` is the right type; using a number rather than text lets the stream code compare and total these values later.

lines.code: public Player(String name, String position, int goals) {
lines.text: The constructor is the only way to build a `Player`, which guarantees every object has all three pieces of data from the moment it exists.
`this.name` refers to the field while plain `name` refers to the constructor parameter, so this copies the incoming value into the object.
A getter gives read-only access to a private field. Stream code calls methods like this through method references such as `Player::getName`.
This getter is what a grouping pipeline uses as the classifier, turning the position text into the key of each group.
Comparators for finding the top scorer are built from this getter, for example `Comparator.comparingInt(Player::getGoals)`.
This annotation tells the compiler you mean to replace a method inherited from `Object`, so a typo in the method name becomes an error instead of a silent bug.
Overriding `toString` means printing a `Player`, or a whole list of them, shows readable details instead of a memory address.
`'\''` is the escape sequence for a single-quote character, so the name appears wrapped in quotes in the output.
